[sakt-p01-v01] Place, entry, form, and mark, and sign indeed; raising, awakening, and wheel-rest indeed — and

[sakt-p01-v02] the arrival at the stage, and the final state indeed; rest, transformation, and the return indeed — and

[sakt-p01-v03] So the doctrine is thirteenfold: the supreme Śākta wisdom, pointed out in every Trika treatise by Śambhu himself.

[sakt-p01-v04] Five fingers below the navel, two fingers above the member — between them lies the place called the bulb, remembered as the station of the wheel.

[sakt-p01-v05] Hold the breath in and out, and cast the mind right there; master the currents of wind completely, and lead them until they enter the middle.

[sakt-p01-v06] This — they say — is entry. Now I will tell the form: a wheel like a horned pond, six-spoked, and steady beyond.

[sakt-p01-v07] The bulb glows like a pomegranate blossom, red by its very nature; this form is declared the third — it consists of contemplation.

[sakt-p01-v08] Set the mind in that middle until it stands steady there; when the wind's hold is released, point out the mark.

[sakt-p01-v09] In the middle of the bulb-wheel stands a digit of the unstruck sound, ringed with lines above and below, coiled like a serpent.

[sakt-p01-v10] Above and below abides her state — sun and moon both; truly she shines, bright as a thousand suns.

[sakt-p02-v11] Gaze at her, at śakti, with a light sealing of the breath; this is the sign pointed out — beyond it lies raising.

[sakt-p02-v12] On the practiced out-breath, utter the mantra; contemplate her awakened — the Supreme Goddess, straight as a staff.

[sakt-p02-v13] Come from the heart of the base, she has entered the suṣumnā road; this is raising declared — beyond it, awakening.

[sakt-p02-v14] Rooted in the bulb, pierce the navel, then the grandsire in the heart; in the throat the unfallen one, Rudra face to face on the palate's floor.

[sakt-p02-v15] At the brow's middle, Īśa; at the door of brahman, Sadāśiva; wake them and rise swiftly to the state that rests on nothing — Śiva.

[sakt-p02-v16] This awakening is pointed out. Then the resting in the wheels: a petal by nature, blazing, flowing, like the steady sky.

[sakt-p02-v17] Nectar, the crest, śakti-brahmā — and the drop-sound: so the twelvefold wheel is proclaimed, says tradition.

[sakt-p02-v18] Piercing in turn — śakti in wheel after wheel, at every instant — she, the Great Goddess, comes to rest: the supreme wheel-rest.

[sakt-p02-v19] First the heart trembles, and the palate gate; his head spins — the sign of the sight's crossing over.

[sakt-p02-v20] It sets each limb spinning, joint by joint; his heart churns — such is the power of true knowing.

[sakt-p03-v21] Whatever changes the state brews in a man — in none of them is there anything to fear; the Supreme Goddess is at play.

[sakt-p03-v22] Drunk on nectar, she brews change upon change — the triple-stain ferment of what was done through many births.

[sakt-p03-v23] She shakes the stained souls loose from the snare, risen from supreme power; this is the arrival at the stage — and the final state is told.

[sakt-p03-v24] When the crossing comes: hair rising, tears falling, yawning breaking, speech faltering from voices within; knots bursting, the divine shiver of touch, drops throbbing out from the navel bulb.

[sakt-p03-v25] That is the final state declared. And now rest is taught: when śakti wakes and pours from the navel wheel.

[sakt-p03-v26] Then the whole village of the senses sets and stands without; when she, the supreme power, dissolves into the supreme place.

[sakt-p03-v27] Then the knower finds nothing — no other thing to know; śakti rests in Śiva — this is called rest.

[sakt-p03-v28] Where her resting lies, let the mind go there into dissolution; then the self is known in supreme selfhood by those made firm.

[sakt-p03-v29] Become Śiva — the self turns Śiva; that indeed is the turning. And he rains forever the divine nectar that is the life of creatures.

[sakt-p03-v30] Hold the mind there — and the goddess enters again; then the return is proclaimed: thirteen in full.
